title: Combine Two Tables
description:
Table `Person` holds people and table `Address` holds their addresses.

Write a query to report the `firstName`, `lastName`, `city` and `state` of every person. If a person has no address recorded, still report them, with `NULL` for `city` and `state`.

Return the result in any order.
hint: A plain INNER JOIN would drop people with no address. Which join keeps every row from the left table?
outputExplanation: The `LEFT JOIN` keeps all Person rows regardless of whether a matching Address exists. Allen Wang (personId=1) has no address record → city and state are **NULL**. Alice Bob (personId=2) matches addressId=1 → New York City, NY. Vedant Deo (personId=3) matches addressId=2 → Leetcode, California. Three rows total, one per person.

tests.name: Example
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1,'Wang','Allen'),(2,'Alice','Bob'),(3,'Deo','Vedant');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,2,'New York City','New York'),(2,3,'Leetcode','California');

tests.name: Everyone has an address
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1,'Smith','Ann'),(2,'Jones','Ben');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (10,1,'Austin','Texas'),(11,2,'Reno','Nevada');

tests.name: One person with two addresses
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1,'Kim','Sara');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,1,'Boston','Massachusetts'),(2,1,'Miami','Florida');

tests.name: Orphan address rows
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1,'Lee','Min');
INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,99,'Ghost Town','Nowhere'),(2,1,'Denver','Colorado');

tests.name: Address stored with NULL city and state
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,1,NULL,NULL),(2,2,'Seattle','Washington');
